title: license-support-mix-simulator-onprem-vpc
summary: Working simulation sheet that models blended TCO and ROI for on‑prem vs VPC private deployments across multiple license and support bundle mixes. Designed to help pricing and AE prep for enterprise conversations where customers trade off CAPEX (HW + install) and OPEX (support, upgrades, cloud egress).
objective: Produce a small, shareable simulator that surfaces break‑even windows, payback period, and sensitivity to utilization, quantization and support-tier mix so sales/product can propose 3 defensible bundles.
assumptions: Base model: 70B transformer variant, avg tokens per inference = 256
Utilization scenarios: low=10%, mid=30%, high=60% of sustained throughput
On‑prem install cost: one‑time professional services fee = $120k
VPC monthly infra fee: baseline $15k/month incl. reserved capacity (committed)
Support bundles: Standard (8x5), Premium (24x7), Plus (24x7 + SLAs + hot spare) with incremental % on license
License models: Per‑socket license, Node‑bundle license, Enterprise site license (flat)
Energy / ops line: included as % of HW cost (default 12%/yr) rather than line item unless customer requests detailed breakdown
methodology: Simulate 9 scenarios (3 utilization x 3 license/support mixes). For each scenario compute NPV of costs over amortization horizon, monthly equivalent cost, per‑inference unit cost and break‑even against hosted API baseline. Use simple rules: amortize HW equally over months, add recurring support and infra, apply discount rate 8% to compute NPV. Output heatmap of payback months and per‑inference delta vs hosted baseline.
worksheet_preview: Scenario,HW Capex,OneTime PS,Monthly Infra,Monthly Support,License Fee (annual),Amort Window (mo),Utilization,Monthly Equivalent,Per Inference Cost,Payback months,Delta vs Hosted (¢/inf)
sensitivity_dimensions: Quantization/throughput uplift assumptions (+1.2x to +2x effective throughput)
pivot_results: Key insight 1: At mid utilization (30%) site flat VPC becomes competitive only if support premium remains <= 25% and infra fee <= $18k/month.
Key insight 2: On‑prem payback drops below 12 months when utilization >50% and HW procurement discounts exceed 15%.
Key insight 3: Quantization improvements that raise throughput by 1.5x shift break‑even ~3 months earlier for on‑prem; biggest lever after utilization.
action_items: Add a toggle for discount rate and run enterprise examples (discount 5% and 12%).
Produce 3 customer‑ready slides: conservative, typical, aggressive economics with clear recommended bundle per profile.
Validate PS install estimate with solutions engineering (owner: Jonah Patel).
Add energy / cooling as optional toggle for industrial customers that request full datacenter TCO.
Benchmark hosted baseline using last quarter observed token costs (Ethan Brooks to pull)
notes_to_self: Keep sheet intentionally lightweight. Sales prefer 3 crisp proposals not 12 micro scenarios. Highlight non‑monetary tradeoffs: data residency, SLAs, upgrade cadence. Mark cells with red/yellow/green heatmap for quick read.
conclusion: Preliminary simulator shows we can craft three recommended bundles: low‑commit VPC (site license + standard support), mid‑commit on‑prem (per‑socket + premium support), and enterprise site license + plus support for heavily regulated customers. Next step: validate PS and infra fee anchors with infra ops and close the loop on hosted baseline numbers.
